findings.label: Limb-girdle muscle weakness/wasting
findings.evidence: Patient ambulating with a walker due to proximal muscle weakness

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of the patient ambulating with a walker; the caption explicitly attributes the proximal weakness and mild lower limb contractures to early Bethlem myopathy, supporting attribution despite the article's DMD-mimicry framing.
panels.attribution_text: Alyami et al. Diagnostic Precision in Pediatric Neuromuscular Disorders: A Case Study of Bethlem Myopathy Mimicking Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.97510. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Patient ambulating with a walker due to proximal muscle weakness and mild lower limb contractures typical of early Bethlem myopathy.
in_text_mentions: rred to a tertiary neuromuscular clinic for significant delays in gross motor milestones and a presumptive diagnosis of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. There was no significant family history of neuromuscular disease. Developmental milestones included sitting at 10 months, crawling at 12 months, and independent walking at 20 months. From the onset of ambulation, he exhibited a classic Gowers' maneuver (characterized by pushing on his thighs to stand) and was never able to run (Figure 1). Parents noted progressive calf muscle enlargement from infancy, poor weight gain, and intermittent joint pain.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of the proband in a Bethlem myopathy case report, captioned as showing weakness of eye and lip muscles. B: Clinical photograph of the same Bethlem myopathy proband, captioned as showing weakness of eye and lip muscles and inability to grimace/puff cheeks. C: Axial thigh MRI from the Bethlem myopathy case, captioned as showing markedly enlarged bilateral posterior thigh groups with arrows/stars. D: Axial lower-leg MRI from the Bethlem myopathy case, captioned as showing enlargement of the medial gastrocnemius and anterior tibial muscles.
panels.attribution_text: Li et al. A novel variant of COL6A3 c.6817-2(IVS27)A>G causing Bethlem myopathy: A case report.. Frontiers in neurology 2023. doi:10.3389/fneur.2023.1063090. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Photographs and lower limb muscle magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). (A, B) Photographs of the proband. Weakness of the eye and lip muscles. (C) The bilateral posterior thigh groups were markedly enlarged (star), especially of the lateral femoral muscle edges and central preservation (arrow). (D) Significant enlargement of the medial head of the gastrocnemius (arrow ↑) and the anterior tibial muscles in both lower legs.
in_text_mentions: breathing. Her cardiovascular and respiratory examinations were normal. The bilateral eyelash sign was positive, and the right nasolabial fold was shallower than the left one. She was unable to grimace and puff her cheeks (Figures 1A, B). Mental function and other cranial nerve function tests showed normal values. Muscle weakness in the limbs was asymmetrical (Medical Research Council (MRC). Grades 4/5 proximally and 5/5 distally, and bilateral hip extensors 2/5) without limb muscle atrophy. Beevor's sign was positive. Her sensations were normal, and muscle stretch reflexes were not elicited.
